- **Google Messages**: Simple, E2EE when both ends use it (requires Android 8.1+ + iOS 15+), integrates with SMS fallback.

Sure! Here are a few popular ride‑hailing apps you could choose from, along with a brief snapshot of each so you can pick the one that best fits your needs:

| App | Availability (major markets) | Typical pricing model | Notable features |
|-----|------------------------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| **Uber** | USA, Canada, UK, EU, India, China, Australia, etc. | Base fare + per‑minute + per‑mile (or km); surge pricing during high demand; optional “UberXL”, “Uber Comfort”, “Uber Green” tiers | Large fleet, multiple service tiers, cash‑less payments, transparent pricing estimate before ride, safety tools (Live Check‑In, Safety Tips). |
| **Lyft** | USA (strongest presence), Canada, parts of Mexico | Base fare + per‑minute + per‑mile; surge pricing; optional “Lyft XL” for larger groups | Simple UI, community‑focused branding, “Lyft Pass” subscription option, safety features (Trip Share, Safety Kit). |
| **Grab** | Southeast Asia (Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Vietnam, Philippines, etc.) | Metered fare; promotions & discounts; surge pricing in some cities | Multi‑modal options (ride‑hail, food delivery, finance services); strong localization (language support, local payment methods). |
| **Didi** | China, Latin America (Mexico, Brazil), select African & Middle‑East cities | Metered fare; promotions; peak‑time surges | Large driver network in China; integrated services (food, parcel delivery, bike‑share); strong safety & verification. |
| **Ola** | India, Russia, Kazakhstan, Australia | Base fare + per‑km + per‑min; promotional offers; peak‑time surges | “Ola Auto” for metered autos, “Ola Shared” for pooled rides; local payment options (UPI, cash). |
| **Bolt** | Europe, Africa, Latin America, Middle East | Metered fare; discounts & promo codes; surge pricing | Fast onboarding for drivers, competitive pricing, simple fare estimate. |
| **DiDi** (same as Didi above) – just to avoid confusion, some regions list it as “Didi Chuxing”. | — | — | — |

### How to pick the right one for you
1. **Geographic focus** – If you’re in the U.S. or Canada, Uber or Lyft are the most ubiquitous. In Southeast Asia, Grab dominates; in China, Didi; in India, Ola; in Europe/Africa, Bolt often works well.
2. **Service type** – Want pooled rides to save money? Uber Pool, Lyft Shared, Grab Shared, Ola Shared, and Bolt Shared all offer that. Need a larger vehicle (3‑4 passengers or a cargo area)? Look for “XL”, “Comfort”, or “Cargo” options.
3. **Payment preferences** – Some apps support local payment methods (e.g., UPI in India, Alipay/WeChat Pay in China, local bank transfers in Africa). Others rely more on credit/debit cards and cash pickups.
4. **Safety & trust** – All major apps have driver‑verification, ride‑tracking, and safety‑share features. Check recent user reviews or the app’s safety page if you have specific concerns.
5. **Cost vs. convenience** – Prices can vary by city and time of day due to surge. If you frequently ride during off‑peak hours, the baseline fare will be lower. Promotions (first‑ride discounts, referral credits) can also sway the choice.

### Quick recommendation (if you’re looking for a universally available, well‑known option)
- **Uber** – Broad global reach, multiple service tiers, strong safety tools, easy price estimate before you request a ride. Good if you travel frequently across cities or countries where Uber operates.
